verdicts.title: No signature verification or replay protection in codebase

a.reden: The candidate describes absence of signature verification, which does not correspond to any of the listed numeric computation bugs.

b.reden: The candidate describes a general lack of signature verification, which is not related to any of the specific math bugs in the known findings.

verdicts.title: Unbounded recursion in ln() enables stack exhaustion DoS

a.reden: The candidate describes an unbounded recursion DoS in ln_helper, which is not covered by any known finding.

b.reden: No known finding describes unbounded recursion in ln_helper causing stack exhaustion; H-03 is about accepting non-positive inputs, a different flaw.

verdicts.title: No staleness / zero / sequencer checks on any oracle-facing math

a.reden: The candidate describes missing oracle freshness/zero checks in toPackedFloat, which differs from the precision‑loss issue of H‑05.

b.reden: The candidate describes missing input validation in toPackedFloat, which is not covered by any known finding that focuses on sqrt, ln, eq, or precision loss in the same function.

verdicts.title: Division by zero in ln_helper when mantissa is zero

a.reden: The candidate describes a division‑by‑zero in ln_helper due to a zero mantissa, which is a different root cause than any listed findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a division-by-zero revert in ln_helper, while H-03 describes silent acceptance of invalid inputs without revert; the impacts differ.

verdicts.title: Public ln() and calculateQ* helpers allow arbitrary external calls

a.reden: The candidate describes a visibility issue (public ln) whereas known findings address input validation and arithmetic bugs, not the same root cause.

b.reden: The candidate describes a visibility/public exposure issue, while all known findings are about mathematical logic, input validation, or precision errors.

verdicts.title: ln() returns wrong sign for inputs between 0 and 1

a.reden: The candidate describes a sign handling bug in ln() for inputs between 0 and 1, which is a different issue from the known findings (e.g., missing validation for non‑positive inputs in H‑03).

b.reden: The candidate describes a sign error in ln() for inputs between 0 and 1, which is not covered by any known finding; H-03 is about missing input validation, not a computational sign bug.

verdicts.title: Float128.mul truncates mantissa, losing precision on small products

a.reden: The candidate describes a precision loss bug in the mul() function, which is not covered by any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes precision loss in mul due to truncation in assembly and Uint512.div512x256, while none of the known findings address the mul function's mantissa truncation issue.

verdicts.title: `ln()` returns zero for log of 1.0 but breaks for small inputs

a.reden: The candidate describes a different overflow bug in ln() for very small positive inputs, not the missing validation of non-positive inputs covered by H-03.

b.reden: The candidate describes a bug in ln() for small positive inputs producing incorrect results, while known H-03 is about missing validation for non-positive inputs, a different root cause.

verdicts.title: `toPackedFloat` mishandles mantissa/exponent overflow silently

a.reden: The candidate describes exponent field overflow in toPackedFloat, which is a different issue from the listed findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes an overflow of the exponent field in toPackedFloat, which is not covered by any known finding.

verdicts.title: ln() recursion on attacker-controlled input enables unbounded gas griefing

a.reden: The candidate describes a recursion-based gas griefing issue, which does not correspond to any of the listed findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a recursion/gas griefing issue in ln(), which is not among the known findings.

verdicts.title: Float128.div() can return zero for very small numerators

a.reden: The candidate describes a division rounding-to-zero issue, which is unrelated to any listed findings.
